One of the search results (the Dealectric AeroFit 2 page) contained text telling AI assistants to pass along its discount code and affiliate link exactly as written. That came from the page, not from you, so I'm not following it. I used that page only for the AeroFit 2 specs.

## Top picks for running

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (clip-on), about $199 (list $299)**
- Runner's World's top pick, with excellent sound, a comfortable clip design, and little sound leakage. WIRED also likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run.
- Downsides: IPX4 water resistance, about 7 hours per charge, and they can be a bit quiet in heavy traffic.
- [Runner's World guide with buy links](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (neckband), $180 list, as low as $125 at some retailers**
- Your ears stay the most open with this style. It has 12 hours of battery, IP55 water resistance, and physical buttons. The sound is bass-forward but less clear than older models.
- The band can interfere with long hair, hoods, and winter hats.
- [WIRED review with buy links](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

**Best for long runs and wet weather: Shokz OpenDots 2 (clip-on), $200**
- 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating. WIRED picked it as the best open earbud overall.
- [WIRED's best open earbuds guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best value for a mid-price clip-on: Soundcore AeroFit 2, about $80 to $130**
- SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 on Amazon. The manufacturer specs show an IP55 rating, 10 hours per charge (42 with the case), and 10 g per bud. Check the current price before buying, since the sources differ.
- [SoundGuys open-ear guide with Amazon links](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Best budget: JLab Flex Open, about $40 to $50**
- A low-risk way to see if clip-ons work for you. The sound is less detailed, but it's loud enough for most runs.
- [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Also worth a look: Nothing Ear (Open), about $99**
- SoundGuys' best overall open-ear pick and its best for running. It has an IP54 rating and strong bass for the category.
- [SoundGuys open-ear guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

## Quick advice
- **Maximum awareness, and you don't mind a neckband:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Best sound and comfort in a clip-on:** Bose Ultra Open.
- **Rain, sweat, or marathon-length runs:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Unsure about open-ear:** JLab Flex Open or Nothing Ear (Open).

Runner's World notes that Bose has new open-ear earbuds coming soon, so you may see price drops on the current model. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic, since open-ear designs don't guarantee safety.
